scope: Deepen ACAD_TABLE/FIELD wire-format and graph-readiness research; refresh open-source peer boundaries for table handling and ACIS carrier reading without changing support claims.

method.kind: Autodesk DXF references, local ODA Open Design Specification v5.4.1, current peer project documentation/issues/release notes, and read-only local source inspection
method.sourcePinning: Public peer manuals, issues, discussions and release pages are mutable. No peer executable or current-master revision was built or run. ACadSharp v3.6.51 release notes are a candidate route pin, not an executed result.
method.evidenceRule: Autodesk documents DXF tags; ODA v5.4.1 governs DWG layout. Peer self-reports identify their own boundaries and candidate probes only. Local parse/write presence does not establish adapter retention or interoperable output.

evidence.topic: ACAD_TABLE references and FIELD graph shape
evidence.observed: TABLE group 342/343/340/331/300/344 encode style, block ownership, block cell, ATTDEF/value and FIELD references. FIELD has hard-owned child fields (360), soft object references (331), and structured cached/data values.
doesNotEstablish: that every producer emits identical optional FIELD fields or ordering
that a parser's FIELD callback is retained by a consumer adapter
that group 344 alone describes the separate NOD FIELDLIST or entity extension-dictionary edges
that field expressions are evaluated or resolve to correct application values
evidence.planUse: Require a bounded graph closure for group 344, preserving owners and remapping all outgoing references; audit the separate NOD FIELDLIST and entity extension-dictionary edges for the admitted producer profile.

evidence.topic: AutoCAD FIELDLIST NOD and extension-dictionary lifecycle
evidence.observed: The Autodesk developer article says a drawing containing fields has an ACAD_FIELDLIST entry in the NOD, that the object is AcDbFieldList, and that each AcDbField is typically accessible through an entity extension dictionary. It describes an AutoCAD R19-era API route and says FIELDLIST is not exposed by the referenced ARX/.NET API.
doesNotEstablish: a universal requirement across every DXF/DWG producer and version
exact field-list membership order or duplicate handling
that a TABLE-specific 344 association can replace the global field index
evidence.planUse: Model NOD ACAD_FIELDLIST membership and the entity extension-dictionary owner as distinct edges for the AutoCAD profile; validate against producer-origin samples and keep deviations explicitly versioned.

evidence.topic: Autodesk FIELD schema versus local typed DXF mapping
evidence.observed: Autodesk's FIELD DXF schema lists groups 301 and overflow 9 as the format string, with 98 as its length. ODA Open Design Specification v5.4.1 section 20.4.76 instead assigns 301/9 to the value string and 98 to value-string length; section 20.4.99 separately specifies nested R2007+ CadValue format/value tags 300/302. Local code writes m_formatString at 4 and m_valueString at 301, and parses 4 as format and 9/301 as value. An available ODA-converted sample has empty root 301 and 98=0, so it cannot discriminate the competing assignments. This is a primary-source conflict, not a proven local bug or interoperable profile.
doesNotEstablish: which root 301/9/98 assignment a producer emits when format and cached values are non-empty
whether the local mapping is intentional for a specific producer/version
that a generated local read/write test would match Autodesk or another producer
that undocumented extra evaluation-state fields are invalid in all DXF versions
evidence.planUse: Treat this as a normative-source conflict. Keep FIELD-backed TABLE writing blocked and do not change mapping based on either document alone. Use literal controls for both grammars plus producer-origin DXF with non-empty format and cached values; record product/build/save version and expected loss. Assert groups 4, 9, 98, 301 and nested 300/302 separately; never use codec self-round-trip as the schema oracle.

evidence.observed: The bundled LibreCAD fork currently maps group 4 to FIELD format, groups 9/301 to value string, and 98 to value-string length; its writer emits 4/301/98, matching this upstream worktree.
doesNotEstablish: an independent normative interpretation because the bundled fork is a related implementation lineage
AutoCAD acceptance or producer-origin semantics for non-empty root format and cached values
that changing the shared mapping would preserve existing LibreCAD consumer behavior
evidence.planUse: Treat the current mapping as a compatibility profile, not a support claim. Keep the in-tree adapter fail-closed; if evidence requires a different wire mapping, add an explicit profile/version gate or safe refusal and preserve a LibreCAD compatibility test.

evidence.observed: Autodesk warns applications not to depend on the reference table's displayed group-code order and calls for code-driven dispatch.
doesNotEstablish: that repeated per-cell sequences can be arbitrarily reordered without changing their meaning
a canonical ordering for all optional or version-specific TABLE fields
evidence.planUse: Test reordering of independent singleton fields while preserving repeated cell-major value/reference sequences. Do not sort the tag stream.

evidence.observed: ODA v5.4.1 describes TABLE geometry in anonymous *T blocks, legacy R21 structures and linked TABLECONTENT/round-trip data, and R24+ DWG with embedded AcDbTableContent while DXF may carry old and new forms. TABLECONTENT supports multiple contents per cell.
doesNotEstablish: undocumented per-version fields beyond the specification's stated limits
a real producer's exact object layout without a trace
visual table rendering or a native editor's acceptance
evidence.planUse: Keep AC1021 and AC1024+ implementations as separate evidence lanes and require an eligible sample trace before DWG parseDwg changes.

evidence.observed: The current manual marks TABLE, TABLECONTENT and TABLESTYLE as broken/undertested and qualifies TABLE/TABLESTYLE as working only pre-2010.
doesNotEstablish: that every LibreDWG release has identical behavior
a runtime pass/fail on the local table profile
a normative format restriction
evidence.planUse: Treat this as a version-scoped peer limitation; do not use the peer as the blanket AC1024+ TABLE oracle.

evidence.observed: The maintainer reports ACAD_TABLE tag preservation and a helper for extracting simple cell text; the general object is not a fully editable typed table and its xref copying remains unsupported.
doesNotEstablish: full table field/style/merge/block semantics
graph-aware copy and handle remapping
native rendering or output application acceptance
evidence.planUse: Use ezdxf only for raw-tag and limited extraction comparisons, not full typed TABLE support.

evidence.topic: ACadSharp table and ACIS comparator boundaries
evidence.observed: The maintainer describes table read as partial; issue #995 reports DWG/DXF table writers unsupported at the reviewed snapshot. v3.6.51 release notes list reading ACIS payloads for 3DSOLID/REGION/BODY and reading the AcDs payload-area offset.
doesNotEstablish: current behavior of an unpinned latest branch
complete TABLE semantics or writer behavior
AcDs handle-to-record association for arbitrary inputs
valid ACIS B-rep geometry or independent-kernel semantics
evidence.planUse: At one composed checkpoint, pin a suitable ACadSharp release to compare structural carrier extraction and versioned behavior; keep semantic shape evidence independent and never run the peer in every fast slice.

evidence.observed: At the original research snapshot the graph precheck was TABLE-root-only. The current local adapter still retains typed FIELD/FIELDLIST callbacks and raw carriers separately, and its fresh-DXF receipt verifies bounded typed/raw count and class/handle/source-version/owner pairing. The precheck has since been generalized to validate the global FIELDLIST through TABLE and non-TABLE extension-dictionary roots, acyclic owner-matching children, and object/CadValue references whose targets exist in the current adapter candidate inventory. fileExport remains fail-closed because no qualified FIELD serializer is invoked; TABLE writing independently refuses nonempty group-344 field handles.
doesNotEstablish: producer-qualified AutoCAD graph behavior or proof that locally inventoried reference targets are actually emitted and remapped
semantic FIELD wire mapping, complete output handle closure, or FIELD serialization
that parser/writer code is interoperable or that FIELD serialization is implemented
a table support claim beyond the existing bounded text/block-cell slice
evidence.planUse: Keep the adapter fail-closed for any FIELD/FIELDLIST carrier. The generalized precheck is a bounded candidate-graph gate, not output closure. Next qualify its graph profile with producer-origin input, inventory all emitted targets, prove one-time reference remapping and post-write closure, and retain TABLE group-344 refusal until schema and writer tests pass.

implementationReadiness.nextSlice: 7G.3d.2c: qualify the generalized bounded candidate graph against producer-origin input; inventory every outgoing handle target against records actually emitted, prove single remapping and post-write closure, and keep export refusal until FIELD wire semantics/serialization are qualified
implementationReadiness.wireGate: Resolve the Autodesk-versus-ODA v5.4.1 conflict over root FIELD groups 301/9/98 using literal controls and producer-origin DXF with non-empty format and cached values; record producer/build/save version and expected loss before enabling FIELD writing
implementationReadiness.fieldGraphPrecheck: Implemented as a bounded fail-closed AutoCAD candidate-graph precheck covering global FIELDLIST members rooted by TABLE and non-TABLE entity extension dictionaries, owner-matching acyclic children, and object/type-64 CadValue handles whose targets exist in the adapter inventory; producer qualification, actual writer emission/remapping, and serializer remain unqualified
graphGate: TABLE 344 targets exactly one retained FIELD
AutoCAD field profile retains the NOD ACAD_FIELDLIST membership and entity extension-dictionary owner as distinct edges
FIELD 360 child ownership recursively closes within bounds and has no cycles
FIELD 331 and object-valued cache references target admitted/remapped output records
owner, reactors, extension dictionaries, custom-class metadata and counts are preserved or safely refused
post-write parseback confirms each handle edge and field semantic separately
implementationReadiness.fastValidation: Per slice: touched strict build, one focused in-memory test, relevant LibreCAD/LibreCAD_3 compile check, git diff --check. Peer/native/full-suite checks remain composed checkpoints.
implementationReadiness.fixturePolicy: Zero new committed DWG/DXF fixtures; authored controls remain literal/in-memory or temporary producer outputs.
